Reframed through the lens of the macro-finance literature, the July 29, 2020 FOMC statement pairs a clearly negative near-term outlook with policy actions that theory and evidence suggest can materially mitigate the downturn. Maintaining the policy rate at the zero lower bound and committing to do so until maximum employment and 2% inflation are in sight is consistent with New Keynesian prescriptions under large negative output gaps and subdued inflation (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor principle). Expanding Treasury and agency MBS/CMBS holdings and continuing repo/ON RRP operations lever the credit and term-premium channels, supporting market functioning and the transmission of policy to broader financial conditions (Bernanke-Gertler credit channel; Federal Reserve influence on the slope of the yield curve). This mix of forward guidance and balance-sheet policy also helps avoid the deflationary steady state emphasized in ZLB analyses (Benhabib, Schmitt-Grohé, and Uribe) by anchoring inflation expectations near target and lowering real rates. Netting these literature-backed mitigants against the statement’s emphasis on “considerable risks” from the public health crisis yields a moderately negative but less severe tone than a purely outlook-based reading.
